summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "add user preferences storage" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran the full question/approach flow, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, presented it for approval before writing any implementation code, and moved on to writing-plans only after I said "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is directly supported by observed screen text, session-log content, and on-disk files. The agent escalated correctly to the architectural path, wrote and surfaced a spec before coding, and began implementation planning only after approval.

observations.description: The Codex spec gate did not work: agent reported 'Verdict: none. The gate did not converge; it exited on an unrecovered incomplete... both captures were empty ({}) and verdict-normalize --require-coverage returned incomplete for each... Recovery found no job at all in status --json'. The agent attributed it to the codex-plugin-cc 0.0.0-stub. Spec therefore got no independent review. Agent handled it honestly ('that is absence of a review, not approval'), but the gate itself is broken in this environment.

Agent added a .gitignore covering docs/hyperpowers and docs/superpowers, which means the spec document it just wrote is git-ignored and will never be committed. That seems at odds with the spec being a durable artifact, and it is the only file left as an untracked repo change.

Claude Code launch showed theme / security-note / trust-folder / bypass-permissions dialogs despite the HOWTO stating dialog-bypass state was seeded; four extra confirmations were required before the prompt.

Multi-select question widgets require navigating past all options to a 'Submit' row and then a second 'Submit answers' confirmation screen — noticeably heavier than the single-select prompts for a one-item answer.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: `grep -o 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' *.jsonl` returned multiple hits including `"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}]` in the project jsonl, before any file writes.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in log: '**Classification: architectural.** "Preferences storage" names a subsystem this repo doesn't have ... so I'll run the full process: questions, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec.' File on disk: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-user-preferences-storage-design.md (ls output).

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code written
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-user-preferences-storage-design.md ... Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write the implementation plan.' At that moment `git status --short` in the workdir showed only `?? .gitignore` — no changes to app.js/index.html, and no preferences.js/test dir in `ls -R`.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Only mention of 'bounded' in assistant text was the optional offer ('Say the word if you'd rather I treat it as a bounded change') and an unrelated 'bounded recovery' step; a committed spec file exists at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-user-preferences-storage-design.md.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: jq over assistant text messages grepping 'spike' returned no classification hit; classification line explicitly says 'architectural'.
